# Music of the 70s
> Discover, Explore and Relive the Greatest Decade in Music

Sitemap: https://musicofthe70s.net/sitemap.xml

## Tools
- [70s Decade Wheel](https://musicofthe70s.net/pages/70s-decade-wheel): Spin the wheel and land on a year from 1970 to 1979. Discover that year's biggest hit, top artists, and defining moment in music history.
- [70s Mood Song Matcher](https://musicofthe70s.net/pages/mood-song-matcher): Answer 3 quick questions and get matched with the perfect 70s song for your mood. Rock, disco, soul, country — there's a 70s song for every feeling.
- [70s Music Trivia Quiz](https://musicofthe70s.net/pages/70s-trivia-quiz): Test your 70s music knowledge. 10 questions on rock, disco, soul, country and more — new questions every round.
- [Random 70s Artist Picker](https://musicofthe70s.net/pages/random-artist-picker): Spin and discover a random 70s artist or band from 605 verified acts — rock, disco, soul, funk, country, punk and more.
- [Random 70s Song Generator](https://musicofthe70s.net/pages/random-70s-song): Spin and discover a random iconic 70s song — artist, year, genre and a direct YouTube search link. Rock, disco, soul, country and more.
- [What Was #1 The Week You Were Born?](https://musicofthe70s.net/pages/birthday-number-one): Enter your 1970s birthday and discover what song topped the Billboard Hot 100 the week you were born. Your personal piece of music history.

- [Glam Rock in the 70s: Britain's Charts, America's Silence](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/genres/glam-rock-in-the-70s/index.html): Glam rock in the 70s ruled British charts but barely touched America's. See the real 16-artist roster and the data behind the gap.

- [Disco Music of the 70s: The Year It Peaked and Nearly Died](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/genres/disco-music-of-the-70s/index.html): Discover the real story of Disco Music of the 70s: its true chart peak, the riot that tried to kill it, and the artists who built the sound.

## Artists
- [Donna Summer: The 1977 Hit Too Influential for the Charts](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/donna-summer/index.html): Donna Summer's I Feel Love peaked at only #6 and never touched Billboard's year-end top 100. Her real, chart-verified 1970s story.
- [Al Green: The Hit He Gave Away Before It Was a Hit](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/al-green/index.html): Al Green landed three songs in one year-end chart, then never released his own version of a song that later became a standard. The real 70s story.
- [Marvin Gaye: The Party Tape That Ended Up in Federal Court](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/marvin-gaye/index.html): Marvin Gaye recorded a #1 hit at a house party in 1977. Decades later it became one of pop music's biggest copyright lawsuits.
- [Rick James: The Motown Deal That Took Eleven Years](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/rick-james/index.html): Rick James got signed to Motown in 1966, then arrested weeks later. The real story of his eleven-year road back to Come Get It! in 1978.
- [George Clinton: One Contract Dispute Built Two Bands](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/george-clinton/index.html): George Clinton split one band into two to dodge a bad record contract. The real 70s story behind Parliament, Funkadelic, and the Mothership.
- [Jim Croce: The Song He Released the Day After He Died](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/jim-croce/index.html): Jim Croce died September 20, 1973. His next single shipped one day later. The real timeline of his final year, verified against Billboard's own chart data.
- [Carole King: The Same Chart, Three Different Names](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/carole-king/index.html): Carole King topped the 1971 year-end chart as a performer, and showed up twice more as the writer behind two other artists' hits that same year.
- [Willie Nelson: The Songwriter Who Became the Star](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/willie-nelson/index.html): Willie Nelson spent a decade writing hits for other singers. See how a Nashville house fire and one stripped-down album turned him into a star himself.
- [Dolly Parton: The Split, the Songs, and the Lawsuit](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/dolly-parton/index.html): Dolly Parton split from Porter Wagoner in 1974, wrote two career songs in one summer, then got sued for it. Here's the real 70s story.
- [Stevie Wonder: The Deal That Built His Classic Period](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/stevie-wonder/index.html): Stevie Wonder let his Motown contract expire at 21, then came back with full creative control. Here's the 1971 deal that built his classic period.
- [Brian May and Queen: The Guitar Built From a Fireplace](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/brian-may-and-queen/index.html): Brian May and Queen built a signature sound from a homemade guitar, a coin for a pick, and an amp made from junk. Here's how it actually worked.
- [Iggy Pop: The 1970s Collapse and Berlin Resurrection](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/iggy-pop/index.html): Iggy Pop's own band fell apart on a Detroit stage in 1974. See how David Bowie and Berlin turned that collapse into Lust for Life three years later.
- [Benny Andersson: The Real Songwriting Method Behind ABBA](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/benny-andersson/index.html): Benny Andersson taught himself piano by trial and error. See the real backward songwriting method behind SOS and every other ABBA hit.
- [Anni-Frid Lyngstad: Born in Wartime, Found on Live TV](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/anni-frid-lyngstad/index.html): Anni-Frid Lyngstad was born in wartime Norway and raised by her grandmother in Sweden. See the real story before she became one quarter of ABBA.
- [Bjorn Ulvaeus: The Bench Where ABBA Actually Began](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/bjorn-ulvaeus/index.html): Bjorn Ulvaeus led a real Swedish folk group for a decade before ABBA existed. See the park bench meeting that actually started it all.
- [Agnetha Fältskog: The Solo Star Before ABBA Existed](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/agnetha-faltskog/index.html): Agnetha Fältskog topped Sweden's chart as a teenager, years before ABBA formed. See her real pre-ABBA hits and the solo album she made alongside the band.
- [ABBA: The Band That Needed Permission for Its Own Name](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/abba/index.html): Discover the real story of ABBA: the Eurovision win that started it all, the fish company that owned their name first, and what came after.
- [Eagles the Band: The Lineup Swap That Changed Everything](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/eagles-the-band/index.html): Discover the real story of Eagles the Band: the backing-band origin, the disputed name story, and the one-day swap that led to Hotel California.
- [Queen Freddie Mercury: Two Nights That Defined Their 70s](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/queen-freddie-mercury/index.html): Discover the real story of Queen Freddie Mercury: the toothache that accidentally launched punk, and the video gamble that changed music.
- [Grateful Dead in the 70s: The Band the Charts Missed](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/grateful-dead/index.html): Discover Grateful Dead in the 70s: a drug bust that inspired their only real hit, the Wall of Sound, and the night that outlasted the charts.
- [James Brown in the 70s: How He Became the Godfather of Soul](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/james-brown/index.html): Discover James Brown in the 70s: the band that walked out, the album that got rejected, and how he became the Godfather of Soul.
- [Talking Heads: Built From Found Objects, Not a Plan](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/talking-heads/index.html): Discover Talking Heads: the stolen TV term that became their name, the Son of Sam coincidence, and how they built a sound from nothing.
- [Village People in the 70s: The Disco Act Everyone Missed](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/village-people/index.html): Discover Village People in the 70s: the gay club that inspired it, the Navy near-miss, and the real story behind the Y.M.C.A. arm dance.
- [Bee Gees: The Story of Pop's Most Successful Sibling Act](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/artists/bee-gees/index.html): The full story of the Bee Gees, from a name that never meant &quot;Brothers Gibb&quot; to disco's biggest phenomenon and pop's top songwriters.

## Songs
- [Song YMCA: The Studio Question That Built a Disco Anthem](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/song-ymca/index.html): Song YMCA started with a producer who didn't know what the letters meant, then went on to a National Recording Registry induction decades later.
- [Bad Bad Leroy Brown: The Only Number One Jim Croce Saw Hit](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/bad-bad-leroy-brown/index.html): Bad Bad Leroy Brown topped the Hot 100 for two weeks in July 1973, the only number one Jim Croce lived to see before his death that September.
- [Carole King It's Too Late: Written by a Total Stranger](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/carole-king-its-too-late/index.html): Carole King It's Too Late spent five weeks at number one in 1971, but a poet she barely knew wrote its breakup lyrics in a single day.
- [Jolene: The Chart Record It Finally Broke, 52 Years Later](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/jolene/index.html): Jolene peaked at #60 in 1974. Fifty-two years later, after Dolly Parton's death, it finally broke the Billboard Top 40.
- [Superstition Stevie Wonder: The Hit He Tried to Give Away](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/superstition-stevie-wonder/index.html): Superstition Stevie Wonder wrote as a favor for Jeff Beck. Motown kept it instead, and it became his first Grammy-winning number one.
- [Donna Summer Hot Stuff: The Rock Turn That Won a Grammy](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/donna-summer-hot-stuff/index.html): Donna Summer Hot Stuff hit number one, lost it to the Bee Gees, then took it back. The $35 guitar and Grammy story behind the 1979 disco-rock hit.
- [What's Going On Marvin Gaye: The Accidents That Made It](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/whats-going-on-marvin-gaye/index.html): What's Going On Marvin Gaye built into a classic began as a Four Tops reject. A warm-up sax take, a mixing slip, and a bassist on the floor did the rest.
- [Al Green Let's Stay Together: The Song He Didn't Want to Cut](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/al-green-lets-stay-together/index.html): Al Green Let's Stay Together topped the pop chart for one week and the soul chart for nine. Green argued for two days before he would record it.
- [Killer Queen: Freddie Mercury's First Real US Hit](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/killer-queen/index.html): Killer Queen was Freddie Mercury's deliberate bid for a pop hit, a call girl character study that finally broke Queen in America.
- [One of These Nights: The Eagles' Turn Away From Country](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/one-of-these-nights/index.html): One of These Nights gave the Eagles a second number one and their first chart-topping album, then the lineup that recorded it fell apart.
- [ABBA Waterloo: The Song Written to Win, Not to Chart](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/abba-waterloo/index.html): The real story behind ABBA Waterloo: the scrapped title, the tax law behind the costumes, and the Eurovision rule that let them sing in English.
- [How Can You Mend a Broken Heart: Written in Under an Hour](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/how-can-you-mend-a-broken-heart/index.html): How Can You Mend a Broken Heart, the Bee Gees' first US number one, was written in an hour and never even charted in Britain.
- [Bridge Over Troubled Water: The Gospel Line Simon Paid For](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/bridge-over-troubled-water/index.html): Bridge over troubled water hit #1 for six weeks in 1970. Paul Simon borrowed its title from a gospel song, then paid the singer $1,000 for it.
- [I Will Survive: A B-Side Nobody Wanted to Release](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/i-will-survive/index.html): I will survive was a B-side the label refused to push, written by a songwriter who'd just been fired, recorded by a singer healing from spinal surgery.
- [Seasons in the Sun: The Beach Boys Killed It First](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/seasons-in-the-sun/index.html): Seasons in the sun started as a dark French song about a dying, betrayed man. The Beach Boys recorded it, scrapped it, and called it too wimpy to keep.
- [Stayin Alive: Built on a Magazine Story That Was Fake](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/stayin-alive/index.html): Stayin alive was written for a movie based on a magazine article its own writer later admitted he made up. Now doctors use it to teach CPR.
- [We Will Rock You: How Queen Built a Stadium Chant](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/we-will-rock-you/index.html): The real story behind We Will Rock You: the crowd that inspired it, the drum-riser recording trick, and how Queen built rock's biggest stadium chant.
- [Gimme Gimme Gimme: The ABBA Song America Never Got](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/gimme-gimme-gimme/index.html): Gimme Gimme Gimme hit number one in five countries in 1979. Atlantic Records canceled its US single release outright. Here's the real reason why.
- [Mamma Mia Song: The Story ABBA Almost Gave Away](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/mamma-mia-song/index.html): The mamma mia song almost went to another band, then knocked Bohemian Rhapsody off the UK's number one spot. Its real US peak tells a different story.
- [Take It Easy: The Song Jackson Browne Couldn't Finish](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/take-it-easy/index.html): Take it easy started as Jackson Browne's unfinished song. Glenn Frey completed it, and one line built a real park in Winslow, Arizona.
- [Dancing Queen: The Song ABBA Played for a King First](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/dancing-queen/index.html): Discover the real story behind Dancing Queen: the secret royal wedding premiere, the year-long wait, and how it became ABBA's only US #1.
- [Hotel California: What It Really Means (And What It Doesn't)](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/hotel-california/index.html): Discover the real story behind Hotel California: what Don Henley actually says it means, and why the Satanism theories are wrong.
- [Bohemian Rhapsody: The Song Nobody Wanted to Release](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/bohemian-rhapsody/index.html): Discover the real story behind Bohemian Rhapsody: the label that refused it, the DJ who leaked it, and the four hours that made the video.
- [Don McLean American Pie: The Real Story Behind It](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/don-mclean-american-pie/index.html): Discover the real story behind Don McLean American Pie: the 1959 plane crash, the joke he told for decades, and what he finally revealed.
- [Best Songs of the 70s: The Ultimate Decade Ranking](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/best-songs-of-the-70s/index.html): Discover the best songs of the 70s, from Debby Boone's record-breaking ballad to the Bee Gees' nine number-ones and disco's commercial peak.
